findings.title: [P2] Official verification searches the wrong provider page before reaching the corrected epoch predicate
findings.rationale:
Source-confirmed counterexample at the very official lifecycle used by the new bounded regression: the real normal create -> authorize -> options -> confirm -> subscribe/authenticated receipt flow selects phone 987654321 on the provider's second page, using after=fixture-page-1 at number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:50-56. It reaches a persisted CONNECTED/RECEIPT_VERIFIED attempt with pairingEpoch=null and a channel with pairingEpoch=0; those assertions are at lines 74-87. The subsequent administrative verify calls at lines 89-90 invoke ChannelsService.verificar. That caller passes only WABA, phone ID and active scoped token to meta.confirmarNumero at channels.service.ts:287, omitting the page cursor. The unchanged fixture at helpers.ts:59-70 searches only its first returned page when after is absent. This excludes the chosen phone and returns null, so channels.service.ts:290 throws PROVIDER_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND before the transaction at lines 317-342 and before convergeReceiptVerifiedAttempt at line 337. This is an inference from exact local source control flow; this reviewer did not execute the request or observe its response code.

This is not only an unrealistic fixture condition. The production MetaHttpClient.confirmarNumero at meta.client.ts:121-127 checks the current scoped grant/WABA and then searches exactly one numerosDaWaba page using its optional after argument. numerosDaWaba limits a page to 100 (lines 105-118). An already authorized, durably owned selected phone outside the first current page therefore has the same conditional availability failure. The existing onboarding confirmation intentionally accepts an explicit page cursor; no such cursor is persisted or supplied by this verify caller. The page size of one in the fixture is a legitimate way to exercise that provider contract, not evidence that all production WABAs fail.

Why it is in this bounded review: it is fresh evidence at the same repeated-verification caller and the newly required official regression, rather than a reopening of the whole unchanged feature. The pagination behavior predates cp36b; the nullable helper does not introduce it. Nevertheless the delivered normal official repeated-verification behavior still cannot be accepted. Root expressly reported that the current frozen final-all run is still returning official [409,409], with its exact conflict code/root-cause diagnosis pending; I did not read that live log. The preserved complete pre-fix API RED also reports [409,409] versus [200,200] and ends at the status assertion. It does not record the official response codes. Consequently that authentic RED is not discriminating proof that this normal test reached, and failed because of, the old numeric epoch predicate. The unchanged page mismatch can produce the same RED both before and after the null-epoch correction. The old NUM-ADH-CP36-01 source mismatch has been removed correctly, but its behavioral/release closure is still unproved and the current official test remains an explicit blocking failure. No privilege escalation or cross-tenant write is demonstrated by this counterexample.
findings.suggested_action:
Keep this source snapshot and all raw RED artifacts intact. Under root-owned scope admission, resolve the official verify path's first-page assumption with a bounded provider-supported verification of the persisted selected phone under the current scoped grant and WABA ownership. Preserve the explicit page-specific onboarding confirmation, real credential use, exact phone comparison, grant/session revalidation, no HTTP inside DB transactions and the existing maximum request/time/lease budgets. Do not solve this by an unbounded WABA scan, global credential, trusting a submitted phone ID, accepting a missing provider resource, or changing the shared provider fake to return every phone. Any adapter path beyond the four frozen correction files needs explicit root admission before a serialized writer touches it; this review authorizes no code change.

Also make the null-epoch regression causal: use a genuine normal official lifecycle whose selected phone can be verified by the declared provider fixture, demonstrate that the pre-correction request actually reaches the epoch conflict (including its safe error code), and prove two successful post-fix verifications with unchanged completed attempt version, receipt, owner/currentAttempt and active credential metadata. Retain a separate explicit second-page verify case so isolating the epoch regression cannot conceal this newly demonstrated caller defect. Do not relabel the existing full status-only RED as an ATTEMPT_STALE reproduction or reconstruct missing details. The Evolution null negative and generation/state/epoch rollback fences must remain.

Preferred A is a narrow caller/adapter correction plus discriminating normal-lifecycle tests, followed by a new frozen package and the appropriate canonical validation and affected independent reviews. Effort is small to moderate; risk is bounded but requires preserving scoped resource proof and request budgets; blast radius is this official verification port/caller and its tests; maintenance and structural soundness improve by removing an implicit first-page precondition. B is to isolate the null-epoch test using a legitimately verifiable first-page lifecycle while retaining this pagination defect as an unresolved same-contract finding; that is lower effort for predicate proof but cannot close the observed page-two failure. C, accepting the still-failing normal lifecycle or weakening provider/epoch proof to make it green, does not meet D-03/D-05/D-07. Root owns final classification and the next admitted correction.
